```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

NIS layouts and coding systems vary across releases. Confirm field definitions,
missing-value conventions, weights, and design guidance in the official
documentation for every year in an analysis. The year ranges below describe
package handling, not exhaustive HCUP release guidance.

## ICD coding systems

The package treats NIS diagnosis and procedure fields before 2016 as ICD-9
and fields from 2016 onward as ICD-10. In 2015, Q1–Q3 use ICD-9 and Q4 uses
ICD-10. The `system` argument selects which slot namespace a flag examines.
Missing version indicators rely on the supplied slot schema; mixed-system
shared columns are not supported. ICD-9 support remains experimental.

## Quarter coverage and annualization

`nis_design(annualize = TRUE)` divides by the number of valid years, not a
fraction of annual coverage. A partial year counts as a full year. If `DQTR`
is available, the function warns about years without four quarters and
2015 cohorts confined to one coding era. Decide whether to exclude partial
years or use another documented convention for the estimand.

## 2023 layout notes

The package keeps `TOTCHG_2023` separate from earlier `TOTCHG` and notes
reported changes in geography and stratum fields. These 2023 layout details
are explicitly unverified against official 2023 documentation and real 2023
files. Do not assume comparability or use these notes as a substitute for
checking the source documentation.

## Check availability in the fixture

`nis_example()` creates invented records for selected years to illustrate
package operations. Its rows are not a complete copy of annual layouts.

```{r years}
path <- nis_example(years = c(2015, 2019, 2020))
nis <- nis_open(path)
nis |> dplyr::count(YEAR) |> dplyr::collect()
```

The summary confirms only that the synthetic fixture contains the requested
years. It does not validate a source year's fields or represent the real
annual file.

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - Pooling years without year-scoped hospital and stratum identifiers.
> - Treating 2015 as a single-code-system year.
> - Assuming fields and coding rules remain unchanged across all releases.
> - Treating package handling of a year as official HCUP documentation.

See [Survey design and weighting](survey-design.html),
[Code transitions and sensitivity](code-transitions.html),
[`nis_open()`](../reference/nis_open.html), and [`nis_design()`](../reference/nis_design.html).
